summary: 58-year-old woman after open hysterectomy/appendicectomy, 36 h colicky pain, bilious vomiting, distension, no flatus; CT: single transition point, no strangulation features. Stable.

inputs.chiefComplaint: Colicky abdominal pain, vomiting and distension
inputs.hpi: 36 hours of colicky central abdominal pain coming in waves, bilious vomiting six times, increasing distension. No flatus for 24 hours, last bowel motion 2 days ago. Open hysterectomy and appendicectomy in the past. No fever. Post-menopausal. No weight loss or change in bowel habit before this.

exam.general: Uncomfortable, dry mucous membranes. Temperature 37.2°C, pulse 96/min, BP 128/76.
exam.abdomen: Distended and tympanic with mild diffuse tenderness. No guarding, no rebound, no peritonism. Lower midline scar. Hernial orifices clear. High-pitched tinkling bowel sounds. Rectum empty on PR.

imaging.name: Abdominal X-ray
imaging.result: Multiple dilated small bowel loops centrally, little gas in the colon.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Small bowel obstruction with a single transition point in the right lower quadrant consistent with an adhesive band; small bowel faeces sign. Collapsed colon. Normal bowel wall enhancement, no closed loop, no mesenteric oedema, no free fluid, no hernia.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Adhesive small bowel obstruction
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Adhesive small bowel obstruction (single transition point, previous laparotomy) without CT or clinical features of strangulation. Non-operative management with water-soluble contrast challenge.

socratesAnswers.associated: Bilious vomiting x6, distension, no flatus for 24 h (constipation)

emergencyLevel.note: Bowel obstruction needs same-day admission; in an outpatient practice this is an ER referral.

mustNotAlarm.note: The exam text says 'No guarding, no rebound, no peritonism'; an alarm for generalised peritonism is a negation error that leads to an emergency-laparotomy prompt.
mustNotAlarm.knownGapNote: Web: computeClinicalPrompts fires 'Generalised peritonism → Perforated viscus' on the substring 'peritonism' in 'no peritonism'.
mustNotAlarm.proposedFix: Negation-aware exam() matching ('no peritonism', 'no guarding', 'no rigidity').

mustInclude.note: Bologna: CT with IV contrast to confirm the diagnosis and look for strangulation (the finding that changes management).
Bologna: operate when NOM fails (no resolution by 72 h) or strangulation develops.

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web: No potassium replacement despite K 3.3: getProtocolByIcd('K56.50') returns the generic bowel_obstruction protocol (prefix K56), not adhesion_obstruction, whose medications include KCl.

mustExclude.note: No appendicitis or peritonitis here: an appendicectomy or emergency-laparotomy template can only come from misread negatives ('no guarding, no rebound').
mustExclude.knownGapNote: Web: Negated exam text ('No guarding, no rebound, no peritonism') triggers both the peritonism prompt ('Emergency laparotomy consent') and the appendicectomy operative-plan prompt.

guideline.name: WSES Bologna guidelines — adhesive small bowel obstruction (2017 update)
guideline.section: CT with IV contrast for strangulation signs; non-operative management (NGT, fluids) up to 72 h without strangulation; water-soluble contrast challenge (colon within 24 h predicts success); surgery for strangulation, peritonitis or failed NOM; virgin abdomen and hernia causes
guideline.citation: ten Broek RPG, Krielen P, Di Saverio S, et al. Bologna guidelines for diagnosis and management of adhesive small bowel obstruction (ASBO): 2017 update of the evidence-based guidelines from the WSES ASBO working group. World J Emerg Surg. 2018;13:24.

rationale: Base case for adhesive SBO. The engines should recognise obstruction, triage urgently, recommend CT, and propose non-operative management (NGT, fluids, electrolytes, water-soluble contrast) with surgery if NOM fails.
